note: The main banks: RBC Royal Bank, TD and Scotiabank, three of Canada's five largest banks and its best-known card issuers whose card terms answered on 2026-10-30 (CIBC's credit card pages sit behind an Akamai check, not circumvented; BMO's didn't answer). RBC: every personal card its All Credit Cards page loads (16; its business Mastercard isn't written), each from the card data file the page loads (read 2026-10-30): the annual fee for the primary card, the yearly purchase rate and the cash advance rate. The RBC ION+ Visa's $48 annual fee is rebated for students or anyone 24 and younger, written as waived under 25 (being a student isn't checked); the RBC U.S. Dollar Visa Gold is in US dollars. RBC's pages state no foreign transaction, over-limit, returned payment or cash advance fee for each card (its Visa Classic Low Rate Option's page names a $5 cash advance fee for its introductory offer; not written), nor a grace period. First-year annual fee waivers that are offers with an application deadline aren't written. TD: its Compare Credit Cards page (annual interest rates, fees and features current as of September 1, 2026): nine personal cards, each with its annual fee, purchase rate and cash advance rate; the TD Low Rate Visa's 0% promotional purchase rate for its first 6 months is written as its intro (6 statement periods, written as 6 months), and its Standard Rate of 24.99% on purchases after two missed minimum payments in 12 statement periods as its penalty rate (its offer terms also name a 13.90% rate for some accounts; the table's 12.90% is written). The TD U.S. Dollar Visa ($39 US a year) isn't written: the page's interest rate cell shows an unfilled placeholder (UDINQEN16), not a rate. TD's information boxes for each card found on its site are from 2023 and give rates TD has since changed, so their other fees aren't written. The four business cards aren't written. Scotiabank: its Credit Card Interest Rates page for each card's purchase and cash advance rates, its all credit cards page for each card's annual fee, and its Credit Card Fees At A Glance (effective February 1, 2026): a cash advance fee of the greater of $5.00 or 1%, a 2.5% foreign currency conversion fee (none on the Passport Visa Infinite+, Passport Visa Infinite Privilege, Gold American Express and Platinum American Express; the U.S. Dollar Visa's conversion fee isn't written), a $29.00 over-limit fee and a $48.00 dishonoured payment fee, all as each card's. The Scotia Momentum Mastercard's 7.99% introductory purchase rate for its first 6 months is written. The Scotia Momentum Visa is written at 21.99% from the rates page, which its card listing gives as 20.99%. The ScotiaGold Passport Visa and L'earn Visa, on the rates page but not offered on the all-cards page, aren't written; nor are the business cards. No bank's page gives a grace period for these cards; the minimum payment is in their disclosures, below. The earlier reading of RBC's Visa Classic Low Rate Option page (2026-10-29) is kept as a source; its figures hold. Minimum payments (wave 5, 30 October 2026): all three banks ask $10 plus the interest and fees (RBC: its More Rewards Visa's information box and its credit card glossary, '$10 plus interest and fees', the whole balance when under $10; TD: the information boxes of its First Class Travel, Aeroplan and Cash Back Visa Infinite cards, '$10.00 + all new interest charges + any fees (excluding the Annual Fee)', which its cardholder agreement (section 4.3) says each card's disclosure sets; Scotiabank: its Gold American Express disclosure statement of August 2016, 'Interest Charges + Fees + $10.00', the newest of its personal card disclosures found, its current pages stating none). Each is written as no share of the balance, the interest on top and $10 added (US$10 on the U.S. dollar cards, the same figure in the account's currency), as the banks ask it, the whole balance where that's less; the fees the banks add on top aren't modelled; the fees on top and any over-limit or past-due amount aren't modelled. Quebec residents' accounts carry a different minimum (RBC: 5% of the new balance or $10, the greater), not modelled; the bank's other-province rule is written.
